name: Turks and Caicos Islands

tax.name: Business Licensing (Turks and Caicos Islands Government)

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: Every self-employed person needs a business licence. The yearly fee runs from US$150 to US$7,500 depending on the occupation.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a sole trader business. The Companies Registry quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
Incorporate the company at the Companies Registry
launchSteps.plain: Only needed for a limited company.

launchSteps.label: Get your business licence
launchSteps.plain: Every business needs one. The yearly fee runs from US$150 to US$7,500 depending on the activity, and the licence expires on March 31 each year.

launchSteps.label: Register with the National Insurance Board (NIB) and the health insurance plan (NHIP)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people choose an income band for their contributions.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer with the NIB
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay National Insurance and health insurance each month.

contributions.label: National Insurance (NIB)
contributions.plain: National Insurance gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people choose an income band, up to US$3,700 a month, and pay 11% of it.

contributions.label: National Health Insurance Plan (NHIP)
contributions.plain: A flat US$250 a month for the self-employed, which can be lower if you can prove income under US$3,000 a month.

calendar.monthlyText: With employees: pay NHIP by the 14th and NIB by the 15th of the following month.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: Renew your business licence (renewals run from February to the end of April).
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay NHIP by the 14th and NIB by the 15th for the previous month.

notes: The Turks and Caicos Islands has no income tax, no corporate tax and no VAT. The costs to plan for are your yearly business licence, your NIB and NHIP contributions and import duty (about 35%) on most goods you bring in.
A 12% tax applies to tourism accommodation.

Business licence fees range from about US$100 to US$7,500 a year depending on the occupation (for example about US$150 for a taxi driver and about US$2,700 for a small architecture firm), and licences expire each 31 March. New business licence legislation was passed in January 2026, so fees and rules may change.
